outcome: The regression run's records are kept as a workflow artifact, so a contributor whose row moved reads the review that moved it on the run page instead of re-running the suite.

acceptance_criteria.text: After the regression step, the fresh result directory `.regression` — its summary and every review file beside it — is uploaded as the `regression-run` artifact of that workflow run, on every run that produced records, including one whose suite failed.

expected_verification.assertion: the run page carries a regression-run artifact holding summary.json and review-001.json

acceptance_criteria.text: The README says where the records are found.

expected_verification.assertion: README.md names the regression-run artifact and where it is found

data_impact: None. The artifact holds the run's own records, which the log already prints.
security_impact: The records go on the run page as an artifact, readable by anyone who can read the repository's workflow runs; they hold nothing the log does not.
rollout: Ships with the workflow; takes effect on the next pull request run.
rollback: git revert removes the upload step; the log keeps printing the rows.
